assumptions: source assumption: object at T1 in uniform-temperature surroundings T2 with gray-surface balance depending on the object emissivity alone (source Eq. 14.44 prose).
Same surface, enclosure pair, and infrared-band emissivity for e, A, To, Ts, P; absolute kelvins required (fourth-power law).
Steady temperatures over the evaluation instant; no participating medium or spectral selectivity beyond the single emissivity.

gaps: Requires extensions: emissivity (1), absolute temperatures (K, offset scale), net radiative rate (W, signed), and fourth-power Stefan-Boltzmann form with inlined sigma. No runtime unit/operator fits.
Linearized heat-transfer-coefficient form h_rad needs a separate adapter, not silently substituted.

models.inverse_notes: P with e, A, and one temperature gives the other temperature via fourth root: To=(P/(sigma e A)+Ts^4)**0.25 requiring a nonnegative radicand and the physical nonnegative root (negative roots extraneous); e=0 forces P=0 regardless of temperatures (reflective limit). Substitution checked: -98.53207283/(5.67e-08*0.97*1.5)+306^4=295^4 within rounding. Inversion does not separate emission from absorption components.
limitations: Excludes convection and conduction, which also transfer energy in real rooms (person example discusses 125 W metabolic vs radiative loss).
Small-temperature-difference linearization and view-factor/enclosure details are outside this record; Earth/atmosphere feedback discussed in source is out of scope.

references.method: Published result: source Eqs. 14.45-14.47 report -99 W for the stated inputs. Replay with the registry stefan_boltzmann value gives -98.538579 W (diff 0.46). Tolerance 1.0 W covers the two-significant display rounding (half unit 0.5 W) plus input rounding.
references.provenance: Published textbook worked example (unclothed person in dark room)

references.method: Independent calculation at a materially different near-ambient pair for an ideal black surface: 5.670374419e-8*1*(300^4-290^4)=58.245519 W. Replay exact in double precision.
references.provenance: Independent elementary illustration of the net-difference form

rejection_cases.reason: Emissivity above 1 contradicts the gray-surface definition (black limit 1); guard e<=1 rejects it.
Surface area A is required; temperatures and emissivity alone do not determine the rate.

relationship.locator: Sec. 14.7, Eqs. 14.43-14.46 with person example (e=0.97, A=1.50, T2=295K, T1=306K gives -99 W)
relationship.original_equation: Q/t = sigma e A T^4 (Eq. 14.43, emission); Qnet/t = sigma e A (T2^4 - T1^4) (Eq. 14.44, net with surroundings T2 and object T1)
relationship.translation_notes: Local e/A map to source e/A; local To/Ts map to source T2 (surroundings) and T1 (object). The Stefan-Boltzmann constant is named as registry constant stefan_boltzmann (5.670374419e-8 W/(m2*K^4), CODATA 2022, exact) per source Eq. 14.43; no variable, input, or family is added for it. Units: e dimensionless, sigma W/(m2*K4), A m2, T K, P W. Dimensional check: (W/(m2*K4))*m2*K4=W. Sign follows surroundings-minus-object (negative = net loss).

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: emission rate is Q/t=sigma e A T^4 (14.43) with sigma=5.67e-08, A area, T absolute kelvin, e emissivity (black 1, reflector 0); net rate with uniform surroundings is sigma e A (T2^4-T1^4) (14.44) depending on object emissivity alone; person example e=0.97, A=1.50, T2=295K, T1=306K gives -99 W net loss.

assumptions: source assumption: electrical power P is effectively constant over the declared operating interval (OpenStax E=Pt with P for time t; EIA one-Watt-for-one-hour definition).
application profile: t is total active operating time in hours within the interval (accumulated on-time); off-period consumption is treated as zero and is not inferred.
Same device/operating condition and the same energy boundary for P and E; device consumption does not by itself establish purchased grid electricity or tariff scope.

constants.locator: Eqs. 20.35-20.36: 60,000 W*h = 60.0 kW*h; EIA example 200 Wh = 0.2 kWh
constants.meaning: watts per kilowatt; converts watt-hours to kilowatt-hours

gaps: Requires vocabulary/dimension extensions: input quantity electrical_power in W, input quantity operating_duration in h, and power*time=energy dimensional rule. Current runtime has electricity_consumption in kWh but no power or hour quantities.
Candidate alias: electrical_power means constant active electrical input power of the device over the declared interval, not instantaneous peak or nameplate alone.

models.inverse_notes: E and positive t determine P = E*1000/t; E and positive P determine t = E*1000/P. Zero-duration guard excludes division by zero for P inversion; zero-power with zero-energy leaves duration underdetermined (any t satisfies 0=0). Substitution checked: E=60, t=1000 gives P=60*1000/1000=60 W. No negative-power branch; export/generation needs a separate signed model.
limitations: Excludes time-varying power (needs load profile or integral over P(t), not expressible in scalar v1).
Excludes losses outside the declared device boundary, standby/off consumption, and tariff/billing rules; energy quantity alone does not establish cost or grid scope.

references.method: Published result: OpenStax Eq. 20.35 reports E=(60 W)(1000 h)=60,000 W*h and Eq. 20.36 reports 60.0 kW*h. Arithmetic replay 60*1000/1000=60 exactly; no rounding beyond the reported one-decimal kWh.
references.provenance: Published textbook worked example converted from reported W*h to kWh by the source itself

references.method: Published result: EIA Measuring electricity states a 40-W (0.04 kW) bulb for five hours uses 200 Wh, i.e. 0.2 kWh. Arithmetic replay 40*5/1000=0.2 exactly.
references.provenance: Published agency example; reported Wh converted to kWh by the source (200 Wh = 0.2 kWh)

rejection_cases.reason: Negative constant power violates the nonnegative-consumption profile; generation/export requires a different signed model.
Operating duration t is required; power alone does not determine energy.

relationship.locator: Section 20.4, Eq. 20.34 (E=Pt) with Eqs. 20.35-20.36 unit step; EIA page sections 'Electricity is measured in Watts and kilowatts' and 'Electricity use over time is measured in Watthours' with 40-W 5-hour example
relationship.translation_notes: Source E=Pt is stated generally (P in watts, t in seconds gives joules; t in hours gives watt-hours). This record specializes units for building-energy accounting: P in W, t in h, E in kWh, with the expression written in canonical base units as E=P*t and the /1000 W/kW prefix step carried by the W/kWh registry unit scales. Pure literal 1000 is the exact W/kW prefix factor (NIST SP 811 prefix rule; OpenStax/EIA examples divide by 1000). Dimensional check: W*h = Wh (energy); Wh/(W/kW) = kWh (energy). No other substitution; constant-power scope retained from source.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: power is the rate of energy use so E=Pt (Eq. 20.34); the billing unit kWh is consistent with E=Pt; students can verify 1 kW*h=3.6e6 J; worked example computes (60 W)(1000 h)=60,000 W*h = 60.0 kW*h and cost at $0.12/kWh.
